status: Register/replace/update concurrency qualified within the stated handwritten-model and separate native-evidence boundaries
evidence_class: Generic finite-execution Lean invariants plus constructive positive/negative model executions; source-reviewed correspondence and actual-store PostgreSQL regressions are separate evidence, not formal Rust/SQL refinement.

paired_counterexample.inputs: Same opaque full payload two-replica seed as the no-op witness: clients0/1, logins10/11, winner2/login12, unrelated login99. Original, replacement and stale-update metadata are pairwise distinct; admitted metadata constraints remain explicit.
paired_counterexample.shared_prefix: Actual old-row/digest preflight and one complete ordinary replacement endpoint constructed under both update-source orders. Registration always retains its fixed real lock/read/compare/upsert/DELETE/create/insert/commit sequence.
paired_counterexample.fixed_branch: Five actual update steps yield rollback and successful acknowledgement, with complete replacement database preserved.
paired_counterexample.original_branch: Six actual update steps begin, miss the old client, stage deployment metadata, request commit, commit and acknowledge. Full final database equals expectedReplacement with only deployment metadata changed to stale; winner row/roles/binding/frame stay identical. Replacement and old update both acknowledge success, update phase is committed, lock is free.
paired_counterexample.events: Actual tags [register1, update0]; the update event contains only deploymentMetadata stale.
paired_counterexample.refutation: Derive a fold from the SAME independent SerialHistory using original request maps, ignoring staged event writes. The serialized current-row update has no client row and must leave replacement metadata unchanged, contradicting the old execution. The counterexample is in actual commit order; no theorem about every alternative serialization order is claimed.

qualified_guarantees: Complete staged register/replace/update programs derived over arbitrary finite mixed executions.
Shared deployment-lock ownership and stability of current metadata/DELETE/matched-row observations.
Exact independent replica/replacement/per-client update effects, preserving complete opaque fields outside each operation.
Independent request-defined effects in actual tagged commit order; confirmed aborted attempts contribute no commit.
Constructed valid normal update, ordinary/instance replacement, replica overlap, partial-write abort and stale-update no-op success.
Two source-mapped original-protocol counterexamples: unlocked replica admission versus replacement, and old missing-row update order.

checks.finite_helper_budget: The existing replacement_seed_steps helper retains its scoped800000-heartbeat allowance; no further limit, premise or source-model change was needed for the paired control.
checks.development_result: The paired control passed its first direct check and final composed build. Earlier no-op proof-normalization feedback is recorded separately in update-replacement-noop.json.

native_evidence.scope: The later native module run passes both actual-store regressions against current22cdabb source, with six instance-registration tests, formatting and strict library Clippy. Old replica baseline source is historical, not claimed identical to the later whole store file. Union of retained original helper/query hashes and newer store/test/design hashes matches current files; both update SQL queries also match22cdabb.
native_evidence.fixture_difference: Native stale-update regression uses one old registration; the Lean witness uses two. Neither substitutes for the other.

limits: One retained deployment and externally admitted namespace/request context. Complete metadata and payloads are parametric; native constraint/crypto validity is not proved by the abstract seed.
PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED atomicity/locking/constraints and typed-store/Core correspondence remain explicit assumptions. No physical SQL or asynchronous Rust extraction is claimed.
An acknowledgement does not preserve a registration against later replacement; exact no-op preservation is for the chosen isolated suffix. Constructed success is not unconditional liveness.
Old update control covers the missing-row order only, not all original successful-row/deadlock behaviors.
Removal/housekeeping, admission/identity reuse, broader authority, service HTTP/audit/reload, callback ingress and deployed recovery are outside this slice.
HUB-REGISTER-01 and the comprehensive Hub goal remain partial/active. Next work connects registration identity to routing, retained Tasks, current authority and SDK recipient checks.
